title: Marketplace integration success hypotheses and experimental playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a tactical, experiment-first playbook for validating partner and marketplace integrations quickly. Goal: find the minimal set of technical, legal and copy assets that deliver first-trial conversions for SMB and ISV partners, with a hypothesis-driven rollout plan.

Status: rough sketch / working doc. Use for partner syncs, not final legal acceptance. TODOs inline.

1) Core hypotheses to test (high priority)
- H1: A 1-click trial provisioning flow + clear SKU copy reduces time-to-first-call-to-action (API key or demo request) by >=40% for ISV partners.
- H2: Showing concrete latency/cost-per-100k-tokens example in the tile copy increases inbound technical leads by 20% vs generic performance claims.
- H3: Providing a short, downloadable architecture snippet (diagram + sample SDK call) reduces technical questions in onboarding by 50%.

2) Success metrics (what we measure)
- Conversion funnel: tile impression -> click -> trial provisioning -> first API call -> paid conversion (30d).
- Time-to-first-call: median hours from click to API call.
- Qualitative: number of technical / legal blockers surfaced during onboarding calls.
- Operational: # of rollback incidents during 30d post-launch.

3) Minimal acceptance checklist (preflight for a partner listing)
- Technical:
  - API contract validated against our example calls (SDK snippet + curl).
  - SSO/SAML integration: optional for enterprise but docs available.
  - Billing SKU mapping: mapped to product catalog and test invoice verified.
  - Security: partner provides SOC2 status or equivalent, or signs data processing addendum.
- Copy & UX:
  - 1-sentence value prop (<=85 chars) and 2 supporting bullets (social proof + use-case).
  - 2 CTA variants: "Start free trial" and "Request dedicated demo" with routing rules.
  - Example pricing blurb and trial limits (token quotas, time-box).
- Legal / procurement:
  - Standard partner agreement template signed or PO process identified.
  - KMS/KV key requirements documented if customer requests private deployment.
- Ops / Support:
  - Onboarding runbook: quickstart docs + link to enterprise enablement checklist.
  - Assigned CSM/SE contact for first 30d.

4) Experimental playbook (how we run fast tests)
- Week 0: intake and quick-accept (1-pager from partner + sample app).
- Week 1: implement minimal tile: imagery + two lines of copy + CTA -> trial provisioning flow.
- Week 2: monitor funnel, log qualitative feedback from first 5 integrations.
- Week 3: iterate on copy (A/B test value prop vs latency/cost examples).
- Success gate: 2 partners convert to paid or show repeatable demo scheduling rate > 40%.

5) Copy templates (quick-start snippets to reuse)
- Hero sentence (short): "Redwood Inference - deterministic latency for production LLMs, with predictable pricing."
- Supporting bullet A: "Scale from dev to dedicated capacity with same API and SLA."
- Supporting bullet B: "Reduce token cost with built-in caching and batching recommendations."
- CTA 1 (trial): "Start free trial — up to 50k tokens, no credit card."
- CTA 2 (enterprise): "Request a dedicated capacity eval"

6) Risk & mitigation matrix (quick)
- Risk: Partner tile promises specific latency but real-world varies. Mitigation: include an explicit note: "Typical latency shown for x86 A100, measured at 64-token median requests."
- Risk: Billing disputes on metered usage. Mitigation: provide a sample invoice and reconciliation path, and sandbox cost estimator.
- Risk: Security gaps for regulated customers. Mitigation: route to Private deployment intake, require HSM/KMS checklist.

7) Required artifacts to publish (min set)
- PNG/JPEG hero image (1920x1080) + alt text.
- 1-line value prop + 2 bullets.
- Trial provisioning playbook (markdown).
- SDK sample snippet (python + curl).
- Billing SKU and test consumption record.

8) Operational playbacks (who does what)
- GTM PM (owner): coordinate partner intake, copy approvals, launch cadence.
- Solutions Eng: verify SDK samples, prepare quickstart.
- Legal: surface exceptions within 48 hours.
- Support/CSM: first 30d onboarding, track issues.

Notes / friction points observed in prior pilots:
- Too much legal back-and-forth usually stalls launch more than technical readiness. Solution: narrow the immediate acceptance list and push non-blocking clauses to post-launch paperwork.
- Partners often ask for sample cost/latency numbers specific to their traffic shape — provide a small 'estimator' snippet and note on assumptions.

Open items / TODOs:
- [ ] Create a lightweight trial cost estimator (mini python script + example). Owner: Marco. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- [ ] Draft a "launch safe harbor" clause for initial marketplace listings to reduce legal delay. Owner: Legal (Sofia). ETA: 2026-04-01.
- [ ] Produce one-page architecture diagram template for tile assets. Owner: Design. ETA: 2026-03-18.

Quick links / references:
- Intake form (internal): https://forms.redwood.ai/g/marketplace-intake
- Prior pilot readout: confluence.redwood.ai/display/GTM/marketplace-pilot-q1
- Slack channel: #marketplace-partners

Conversation starters for partner syncs:
- "What does success look like for you in the first 30 days?"
- "Which environment will you use for initial testing (hosted, dedicated, private)?"
- "Do you require any custom routing or model variants pre-approved?"

Bottom line: prioritize the small set of artifacts that unblock initial usage (trial, SDK snippet, billing SKU) and defer non-blocking legal/procurement items to post-launch. Use this playbook to run 2–3 parallel experiments and lock a repeatable template for future partners.
